acknowledge.text: It's a heavier day. You don't have to pretend otherwise.
Things feel low right now. Noticing it is already a small kindness to yourself.
Low days are hard. Let's keep whatever comes next small and gentle.
This is a really heavy moment. You don't have to do anything with it right now.
That's a lot of weight to feel. Let's take things one small step at a time.

understand.text: Low feelings often come with less energy, so even small things can feel big. Many people find tiny, gentle steps help more than big plans.
Feeling low is often a sign that something needs rest, comfort or company. It says nothing about what you're worth.

options.title: Look after the basics
options.text: Have you had some water, something to eat, a bit of daylight today? Pick just one.
options.why: When energy is low, looking after the body's basics often makes the biggest small difference.

options.title: A few slow breaths
options.text: Breathe in gently and out slowly, following the circle. Nothing else for now.
options.why: Slow breathing can give your body a moment of steadiness, without asking much of you.

options.title: Notice five things
options.text: Look around slowly and notice five things you can see, one at a time.
options.why: Gentle attention to what's around you can give heavy thoughts a short rest.

options.title: One tiny thing
options.text: Choose something that takes a moment: open a window, wash one cup, step outside the door and back.
options.why: A small action can make a little momentum without asking much of you.

options.title: Comfort, on purpose
options.text: A blanket, a warm drink, a familiar song or show. Something that has felt comforting before.
options.why: Choosing comfort on purpose is a way of being on your own side.

options.title: Be near someone
options.text: Send a short message to someone you trust. It can be as simple as "thinking of you".
options.why: Low feelings often make us want to pull away, even though a little connection tends to help.

options.title: Talk to yourself like a friend
options.text: What would you say to a friend who felt exactly like this? See if you can say it to yourself.
options.why: Many people are much gentler with others than with themselves. This borrows a little of that gentleness.
options.prompt: What I'd say to a friend feeling like this:

options.title: Write it down
options.text: What's weighing on you most? A few words is enough.
options.why: Naming what's heavy can make it a little easier to hold.
options.prompt: What's weighing on me most right now:

options.title: A note for later
options.text: If there's a bit of energy, write a short letter to yourself for a day like this, about what helps.
options.why: Your own words can be a comfort when you find them again.

options.title: Talk to someone now
options.text: If things feel too heavy to hold on your own, there are people you can talk to, any time.
options.why: You deserve support, and you don't have to earn it.
